r.정치 구도: The president serves a single five-year term and cannot run again. A military dictatorship that lasted 35 years from 1954 ended in a 1989 coup, yet the Colorado Party that had propped it up has held power almost the whole time since democracy arrived. It has lost a presidential election only once, in 2008, and the president elected then was removed by congressional impeachment in 2012. In November 2026 regulators seized Ueno, a digital bank tied to the president, and the deposits of well over a million savers were frozen. The president had held shares in the bank's holding company and had appointed a figure linked to the bank to head the central bank, and on November 6 the Senate voted to remove him. The vice president took over and will serve out the term to August 2028.

t.why: Landlocked in the middle of South America, Paraguay ships soybeans and grain to the Atlantic on barges along the Paraguay and Paraná rivers. The Itaipu dam, built under a 1973 treaty with Brazil, splits its power in half, and Paraguay sells the electricity it does not use to Brazil. Fifty years after the treaty, the two countries began renegotiating power prices and sales terms in 2023, but the talks stalled for a while over allegations that Brazilian intelligence spied on the Paraguayan side. It has recognized Taiwan since 1957 and is the only country in South America that still does. That keeps an argument going between farm groups who want access to China and governments that want to protect ties with Taiwan and the United States. In 1991 it founded the Mercosur common market with Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay.
t.rel: A landlocked country between Brazil and Argentina. It runs the giant Itaipu hydropower plant with Brazil and the Yacyreta Dam with Argentina, selling electricity. It is a founding member of Mercosur.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations began in 1962. In April 1965 a group of Korean farm immigrants arrived by ship in the capital, Asunción, one of the first chapters of Korean migration to South America. Farming proved hard, so many moved to the city and made a living selling clothes and trading. Many others later moved on from Paraguay to Brazil and Argentina. About 5,000 Koreans still live in the country, mostly in Asunción.
t.know: Thanks to Itaipu, built with Brazil, nearly all of Paraguay's electricity comes from hydropower.
etext: The Itaipu and Yacyretá dams generate far more power than the country uses, and Paraguay sells the surplus to its neighbors. It is using cheap, clean power to court energy-hungry businesses such as data centers.
It ranks among the world's top soybean exporters and sells a lot of beef. When river levels fall, barges cannot sail and exports stall, and in drought years growth swings sharply.
It has built up the maquila system, which draws assembly plants with low taxes and labor costs. They make auto parts and clothing, mostly for Brazil.

Many people work off the books, so the state is small and short of money for roads and schools. The collapse of the digital bank Ueno in November 2026 shook trust in finance, with deposit guarantee costs and feared losses for pension funds.
